title.es: Más allá de said y asked

es: Reconocer verbos de reporte (admit, deny, insist, urge, wonder) que muestran la intención de quien habló y relacionarlos con citas directas.

teaching.en: Tom admitted that he had broken the window.
teaching.es: Tom reconoció que había roto la ventana.
teaching.explanationEs: Admitted: reconoce algo que hizo («Fui yo»). El tiempo retrocede un paso: had broken.
segments: Tom admitted that he
had broken the window.
teaching.audioText: Tom admitted that he had broken the window.

teaching.en: Mia denied that she had taken the last cake.
teaching.es: Mia negó haber tomado el último pastel.
teaching.explanationEs: Denied: niega algo («Yo no fui»).
segments: Mia denied that she had
taken the last cake.
teaching.audioText: Mia denied that she had taken the last cake.

teaching.en: Ana insisted that she was telling the truth.
teaching.es: Ana insistió en que decía la verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Insisted: repite con firmeza lo que dice («¡Es verdad, te lo aseguro!»).
segments: Ana insisted that she
was telling the truth.
teaching.audioText: Ana insisted that she was telling the truth.

teaching.en: The teacher urged us to hurry because the bus was leaving.
teaching.es: La profesora nos instó a darnos prisa porque el autobús se iba.
teaching.explanationEs: Urged + persona + to + verbo: pide con insistencia que alguien actúe.
segments: The teacher urged us to hurry
because the bus was leaving.
teaching.audioText: The teacher urged us to hurry because the bus was leaving.

teaching.en: Leo wondered if the shop was still open.
teaching.es: Leo se preguntaba si la tienda seguía abierta.
teaching.explanationEs: Wondered + if: una pregunta que te haces a ti mismo; sin inversión ni signo de pregunta.
segments: Leo wondered if the
shop was still open.
teaching.audioText: Leo wondered if the shop was still open.

teaching.en: My sister warned me that the road was dangerous.
teaching.es: Mi hermana me advirtió que la carretera era peligrosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Warned + persona + that: avisa de un peligro.
segments: My sister warned me that
the road was dangerous.
teaching.audioText: My sister warned me that the road was dangerous.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase reporta lo que dijo Mia con el verbo adecuado?

choices.text: Mia admitted that she had taken the pen.
Mia urged us to take the pen.
Mia denied that she had taken the pen.

feedback.es: Mia dijo «I didn't take your pen»: niega algo, así que el verbo es denied. Admitted sería lo contrario y urged pide una acción.

hint.es: Fíjate en si Mia reconoce lo que hizo o lo rechaza.

origin.text: «I didn't take your pen!» said Mia.

prompt.es: ¿Qué verbo de reporte encaja con lo que dijo Tom?

choices.text: admitted
denied
suggested

feedback.es: Tom dice que fue su culpa: reconoce algo que hizo, por eso admitted. Denied sería negarlo y suggested, proponer algo.

hint.es: Piensa si Tom reconoce lo que hizo, lo niega o propone algo.

origin.text: Tom says: «Yes, it was my fault. I left the door open.»

feedback.es: Wondered + if recoge una pregunta que alguien se hace a sí mismo.

hint.es: Es el verbo de una pregunta que te haces a ti mismo.

origin.text: Leo ___ if the shop was still open.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la persona con lo que dice.

choices.text: The speaker is admitting something.
The speaker is denying something.
The speaker is urging someone to hurry.

feedback.es: La persona rechaza una acusación («It wasn't me»): eso es denying. No reconoce nada ni pide que alguien se dé prisa.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la versión reportada correcta?

Carlos denied that he had lost the tickets.

feedback.es: Carlos se disculpa y reconoce que perdió las entradas: admitted. Denied sería negarlo.

choices.text: The speaker wondered whether they would leave tomorrow.
The speaker wondered whether they had already left.
The speaker wondered why they had left the house.

feedback.es: I wonder if… se reporta con wondered whether y retroceso del tiempo (had already left). Las otras dos cambian la pregunta.

origin.audio: I wonder if they have already left.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sara prometió que llamaría más tarde.»

feedback.es: Promised recoge un compromiso; would es el retroceso de will.

origin.text: Sara ___ that she would call later.

es: Usar verbos de reporte con su patrón: -ing, to + infinitivo, persona + to + infinitivo, of + -ing y that.

teaching.en: Tom suggested taking a taxi.
teaching.es: Tom sugirió tomar un taxi.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggested + -ing: propone una idea; no lleva persona + to.
segments: Tom suggested taking
a taxi.
teaching.audioText: Tom suggested taking a taxi.

teaching.en: Mia admitted losing the keys.
teaching.es: Mia admitió haber perdido las llaves.
teaching.explanationEs: Admit y deny van con -ing cuando quien habla es el mismo sujeto.
segments: Mia admitted losing
the keys.
teaching.audioText: Mia admitted losing the keys.

teaching.en: Leo promised to call me later.
teaching.es: Leo prometió llamarme más tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Promise, offer y refuse + to + verbo base.
segments: Leo promised to
call me later.
teaching.audioText: Leo promised to call me later.

teaching.en: Ana refused to lend me her bike.
teaching.es: Ana se negó a prestarme su bici.
teaching.explanationEs: Refused + to + verbo: el sujeto es quien se niega.
segments: Ana refused to lend
me her bike.
teaching.audioText: Ana refused to lend me her bike.

teaching.en: The doctor advised me to rest, and she warned me not to work too much.
teaching.es: La doctora me aconsejó descansar y me advirtió que no trabajara demasiado.
teaching.explanationEs: Advise y warn + persona + to + verbo; en negativo, not to.
segments: The doctor advised me to rest, and she
warned me not to work too much.
teaching.audioText: The doctor advised me to rest, and she warned me not to work too much.

teaching.en: Sara accused her brother of reading her messages.
teaching.es: Sara acusó a su hermano de leer sus mensajes.

segments: Sara accused her brother
of reading her messages.
teaching.audioText: Sara accused her brother of reading her messages.

feedback.es: Suggest va seguido de -ing: suggested taking.

hint.es: Después de suggest el verbo no lleva to.

es: Comparar una conversación con su versión reportada y detectar distorsiones de tiempo, persona o sentido.

vocabulary.es: el original, lo que se dijo de verdad

teaching.en: Tom said he was tired then.
teaching.es: Tom dijo que estaba cansado en ese momento.
teaching.explanationEs: Now → then: el «ahora» de la cita original pasa a «entonces»; am → was.
segments: Tom said he
was tired then.
teaching.audioText: Tom said he was tired then.

teaching.en: Ana said she had been there the day before.
teaching.es: Ana dijo que había estado allí el día anterior.
teaching.explanationEs: Here → there y yesterday → the day before; el tiempo retrocede un paso (was → had been).
segments: Ana said she had been
there the day before.
teaching.audioText: Ana said she had been there the day before.

teaching.en: The original was «I might come», but the report says she promised to come, so that version is distorted.
teaching.es: El original era «quizá venga», pero el reporte dice que prometió venir, así que esa versión está distorsionada.
teaching.explanationEs: Una versión distorsionada cambia la fuerza de lo dicho: might no es promised.
segments: The original was «I might come», but the report says
she promised to come, so that version is distorted.
teaching.audioText: The original was «I might come», but the report says she promised to come, so that version is distorted.

teaching.en: She said «a few people», but the report says «hundreds», so it is exaggerated.
teaching.es: Ella dijo «unas pocas personas», pero el reporte dice «cientos», así que está exagerado.
teaching.explanationEs: Exaggerated: hace algo más grande de lo que fue.
segments: She said «a few people», but the
report says «hundreds», so it is exaggerated.
teaching.audioText: She said «a few people», but the report says «hundreds», so it is exaggerated.

teaching.en: An accurate report keeps every detail: who said it, what they said and when.
teaching.es: Un reporte exacto conserva cada detalle: quién lo dijo, qué dijo y cuándo.
teaching.explanationEs: Accurate + detail: no se omite ni se añade información.
segments: An accurate report keeps every detail: who
said it, what they said and when.
teaching.audioText: An accurate report keeps every detail: who said it, what they said and when.

teaching.en: In a faithful version, «I may be late» becomes He said he might be late.
teaching.es: En una versión fiel, «puede que llegue tarde» se convierte en Dijo que quizá llegaría tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: May → might: el grado de posibilidad se mantiene al retroceder.
segments: In a faithful version, «I may be late»
becomes He said he might be late.
teaching.audioText: In a faithful version, «I may be late» becomes He said he might be late.

prompt.es: Elige el reporte fiel de lo que dijo Tom.

choices.text: Tom said I was very tired then.
Tom said he was very tired then.
Tom said he was very tired and wanted to go home.

feedback.es: Fiel: I → he, am → was y now → then. Una versión cambia mal la persona (I) y otra añade información que Tom no dijo.

hint.es: Compara la persona, el tiempo del verbo y la palabra now, y mira si se añade algo.

origin.text: Original: «I'm very tired now.»

prompt.es: ¿Qué reporte respeta lo que dijo Ana?

choices.text: Ana promised to come to the party.
Ana said she would come to the party.
Ana said she might come to the party.

feedback.es: May pasa a might y conserva la posibilidad. Promised la convierte en compromiso y would la presenta como segura.

hint.es: Might mantiene la posibilidad de may; promised y would la cambian.

origin.text: Original: «I may come to the party.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo dijo que vendrían al día siguiente.»

feedback.es: Tomorrow se convierte en the next day cuando reportas en otro momento.

choices.text: Mia said she couldn't come that night because she was busy.
Mia said she didn't want to come that night.
Mia said she couldn't come the next night because she was busy.

choices.text: She said they would see the match the day before.
She said they had seen the match the day before.

feedback.es: Fiel: we → they, saw → had seen y yesterday → the day before. Una versión cambia el tiempo (would see mira al futuro) y otra cambia el día (the next day).

es: Contar una conversación diferenciando afirmaciones, preguntas, promesas y advertencias, con al menos cuatro verbos de reporte distintos.

teaching.en: I want to retell the conversation I had with Ana yesterday.
teaching.es: Quiero volver a contar la conversación que tuve ayer con Ana.
teaching.explanationEs: Retell: contar lo que se dijo, en orden y con tus palabras.
segments: I want to retell the conversation
I had with Ana yesterday.
teaching.audioText: I want to retell the conversation I had with Ana yesterday.

teaching.en: Ana told me that she had lost her phone, and afterwards she asked me if I could help.
teaching.es: Ana me dijo que había perdido el móvil y después me preguntó si podía ayudarla.
teaching.explanationEs: Told me that es una afirmación; asked me if es una pregunta, con orden normal (I could help).
segments: Ana told me that she had lost her phone,
and afterwards she asked me if I could help.
teaching.audioText: Ana told me that she had lost her phone, and afterwards she asked me if I could help.

teaching.en: I promised to help her, but I warned her not to worry too much.
teaching.es: Le prometí ayudarla, pero le advertí que no se preocupara demasiado.
teaching.explanationEs: Promised to: promesa. Warned her not to: advertencia en negativo.
segments: I promised to help her, but I
warned her not to worry too much.
teaching.audioText: I promised to help her, but I warned her not to worry too much.

teaching.en: She complained that her brother never returned her things.
teaching.es: Se quejó de que su hermano nunca le devolvía sus cosas.
teaching.explanationEs: Complained that: una queja sobre algo que molesta.
segments: She complained that her brother
never returned her things.
teaching.audioText: She complained that her brother never returned her things.

teaching.en: Finally, she mentioned that her brother had found the phone under the sofa.
teaching.es: Por último, mencionó que su hermano había encontrado el móvil debajo del sofá.
teaching.explanationEs: Mentioned that: añade un dato sin darle demasiada importancia.
segments: Finally, she mentioned that her brother had
found the phone under the sofa.
teaching.audioText: Finally, she mentioned that her brother had found the phone under the sofa.

teaching.en: At the end of the conversation, Ana told me that the shop closes at six.
teaching.es: Al final de la conversación, Ana me dijo que la tienda cierra a las seis.
teaching.explanationEs: Si lo dicho sigue siendo cierto (la tienda cierra todos los días a las seis), puedes dejar el presente.
segments: At the end of the conversation, Ana told
me that the shop closes at six.
teaching.audioText: At the end of the conversation, Ana told me that the shop closes at six.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión cuenta bien la conversación?

choices.text: Ana said she is late because the bus breaks down, Leo asked if was she coming, and she promised to come at eight.
